papers.title: Can LLMs predict the outcomes of machine learning experiments?
papers.summary: Evaluates how well frontier LLMs can predict the results of machine learning experiments, including ones they propose themselves. The best model reaches an R² of about 0.49, showing meaningful but limited ability to forecast experimental outcomes, with implications for automated research agents.

papers.title: Flat Loss, Evolving Features: Grokking in Modular Addition
papers.summary: Studies grokking on modular addition and shows that generalization can emerge while the training loss stays nearly flat, because internal features keep evolving. Includes a detailed mechanistic analysis plus a one-block transformer experiment.
